name: Feast Of Pentecost The
overview: The Feast of Pentecost, also known as the Feast of Weeks or the Feast of Harvest, is a divinely appointed holy convocation marked by specific sacrifices and offerings as described in Numbers 28:27-31. It is held on the fiftieth day after the offering of the first sheaf of barley, symbolizing the first fruits of the harvest. This feast was not only a time of holy rejoicing and mandatory attendance for all males but also holds profound New Testament significance, as the Holy Spirit was given to the apostles on the day of Pentecost (Acts 2:1). The observance was established to be perpetual, underscoring its enduring spiritual and communal importance for God's people.
